Part II  Nutrition Throughout the Life Cycle
Vitamin D
Vitamin D deficiency, defined based on the serum or plasma measurement of 25-hydroxyvitamin 
D [25(OH)D], is a common and poorly recognized condition that occurs in infants, children, 
adolescents, and adults. Many affected children are dark skinned and have limited exposure to UV 
light, are fed unfortified “health food” milk alternatives, or are breastfed without vitamin D sup­
plementation by mothers with vitamin D insufficiency or deficiency.
